quests.instruction: The story is about how the tenants got their heating fixed. Choose the three statements that give the most complete short retelling.
quests.story: The tenants of Alder House had been without reliable heating since November. Their association collected signatures from forty-two flats and sent them to the landlord, who ignored them for a month. The chair, Mrs. Varga, then invited a local reporter to see the cold flats, and a short article appeared the following Monday. The landlord scheduled a boiler replacement within days. Meanwhile the association's treasurer moved to a new city and handed over the accounts. The new boiler was running by the end of January.
options: A new boiler was running by the end of January.
The association's treasurer moved to a new city and handed over the accounts.
The chair invited a reporter to see the cold flats, and the article pushed the landlord to act.
The tenants collected signatures from forty-two flats, but the landlord ignored them for a month.
quests.hint: Ask which events carry the heating problem to its end, and which belong to someone else's story.
quests.explanation: The treasurer's move is a change inside the association and has no effect on the boiler. The thread runs from the ignored petition, to the reporter's visit and article, to the new boiler.
storyKeyEvents: The tenants collected signatures from forty-two flats, but the landlord ignored them for a month.
The chair invited a reporter to see the cold flats, and the article pushed the landlord to act.
A new boiler was running by the end of January.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that carry the central thread from problem to result.

storyKeyEvents: The university lab had only two working microscopes for sixty students.
The lab manager set up a scheme to share microscopes with the neighbouring college.
By March every student had at least two hours of hands-on time each week.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give the most complete short retelling.
quests.story: The primary school's science week was at risk when the visiting scientist cancelled. The head teacher asked parents whether any worked in science, and a parent who was a chemical engineer agreed to run three workshops. The school hall holds up to two hundred people at assemblies. Science week went ahead with all six classes taking part.
